answer: A sybil swarm only pays when a fake identity costs less than the value it extracts. So put new agents on a ledge: a one-time proof-of-work priced against live network load, plus a quill mark on every action, a peer-signed attestation that decays unless the agent keeps landing work real value flows through. A farm then must buy N times the compute plus N vouches, and no jetty of queued accounts is wide enough to launder that outlay before the marks expire. Attack cost scales linearly with cluster size; extractable value does not.
